title: Make the files this session's splits touched shfmt-clean
objective: Ensure the 250-line splits landed in 41cc045, a84556a and 936e0ec do not add new shfmt violations to linux_configuration, whose shell_check.sh run_linters pass compares every discovered script against shfmt's default formatting.
acceptance_criteria: shfmt -d reports no diff for analyze_repo.sh and for the three new lib/shell_check_*.sh files.
shellcheck still reports zero findings across every file this session created or modified.
analyze_repo.sh still runs to completion (exit 0) against a fixture repo and still produces artifacts byte-identical to the pre-split original at 133fccf.
The STEP 1 comment banner that shfmt -w stripped from analyze_repo.sh is restored, so all eight STEP banners are present.
No file that was already shfmt-dirty before this session is reformatted; the change is scoped to what these splits touched.
out_of_scope: Reformatting the 157 of 298 linux_configuration shell files that already fail shfmt at 133fccf. That drift predates this session and fixing it is a repo-wide formatting decision, not a line-count split.
Making shell_check.sh itself shfmt-clean: it was already dirty at 133fccf, uses 2-space indentation throughout, and reformatting it would rewrite the whole file rather than the seam.
Adding shfmt to .pre-commit-config.yaml or introducing an .editorconfig.
verifier: shfmt -d over the four files (expects no output), shellcheck over every file this session touched (expects zero findings), a stubbed end-to-end run of analyze_repo.sh against a fixture repo diffed artifact-by-artifact against the 133fccf run, and shell_check.sh --skip-install --list-only --verbose piped to a line count (expects 321).
